official.description_text:
: Researcher in computational magnetism and spintronics
Apply for position
School of Engineering Sciences at KTH
Job description
The Department of Applied Physics is seeking a researcher in theoretical and computational magnetism and spintronics. The position is placed in an internationally prominent research group at the AlbaNova University Center, studying magnetic materials and spin phenomena using advanced computational methods.
You will conduct research on magnetic and spintronic phenomena in quantum materials and low-dimensional systems, for example spin and magnon transport, fundamental magnetic interactions, and topological spin textures in two-dimensional magnets, antiferromagnets and altermagnets. The work includes the development and application of first-principles calculations, atomistic spin dynamics and micromagnetic simulations, as well as the development of automated and AI-assisted computational workflows for large-scale materials studies.
The duties also include supervising doctoral students and postdocs, collaborating with experimental and theoretical research groups in Sweden and internationally, actively seeking external research funding, and contributing to the scientific environment of the group and the department. Some teaching and pedagogical qualification may be included in the duties.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree
Documented research expertise in theoretical or computational condensed matter physics with a focus on magnetism and spintronics, demonstrated through publications in leading international scientific journals.
Extensive experience of electronic structure calculations (first principles/DFT) and of simulating magnetic materials and their properties.
Excellent command of English, spoken and written, as the work is carried out in an international research environment.
As a person, you are independent and driven, and you have excellent collaborative abilities.
Preferred qualifications
Documented experience of research on fundamental magnetic interactions, for example the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, magnetic anisotropy and exchange interactions, and their role in topological magnetism.
Experience of studies of spin and magnon transport in two-dimensional magnets, van der Waals materials, antiferromagnets or altermagnets.
Experience of atomistic spin dynamics and micromagnetic simulations.
Experience of machine learning/AI and of developing automated workflows for large-scale calculations on high-performance computing resources.
A documented ability to attract external research funding in competition, as well as scientific prizes and awards.
Teaching ability and experience of supervising doctoral students or postdocs.
The ability to work towards research results being utilised in practice and to inform about research and development work.
Experience of developing and leading activities and staff.
Knowledge of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with a specific focus on gender equality.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system in order to apply for this position. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Max two pages long.
Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The employment is valid until further notice (permanent post) according to agreement.
The employment begins with a six-month probationary period.

ai.summary: A permanent research position in theoretical and computational magnetism and spintronics, involving first-principles calculations, atomistic spin dynamics, and micromagnetic simulations of quantum materials and low-dimensional systems. The role includes supervision, funding acquisition, and teaching in a leading KTH research group.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap. The researcher studies human-centred immersive systems, spatial cognition, collaborative learning, and wayfinding in XR. This position concerns fundamental condensed matter physics—magnetism, spintronics, topological spin textures, and quantum materials. These are pure physics/materials science domains with no connection to HCI, immersive systems, human-centred design, or spatial learning.

methodological_fit.rationale: Both potentially involve computational modelling and large-scale data analysis. However, the researcher's computational work is application-level (Unity game engine, multiplayer systems, user study analysis). This role is fundamental physics computation: DFT, atomistic spin dynamics, micromagnetic simulations, and AI-assisted materials discovery. Methodologies are entirely different.

growth_value.rationale: This position develops expertise in condensed matter physics, computational materials science, and high-performance computing for physics simulations. None of these capabilities advance the researcher's stated goals: designing and evaluating human-centred immersive systems for spatial understanding and collaboration. No capability gap closure.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a prestigious institution in a priority country (Sweden). The Department of Applied Physics is internationally prominent. The position offers permanence and research independence. However, the research group operates in theoretical physics—far outside the target research communities (HCI, immersive systems, spatial cognition). This does not support the researcher's strategic identity or future positioning at target institutions (Aalto, TU Delft HCI groups).

eligibility_flags: Requires doctoral degree in condensed matter physics or equivalent; researcher's MMU MSc by Research in immersive systems does not meet disciplinary expectations

Required qualifications demand 'documented research expertise in theoretical or computational condensed matter physics with focus on magnetism and spintronics, demonstrated through publications'—researcher has zero publications in this domain
Preferred qualifications emphasize specific physics areas (Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, van der Waals materials, antiferromagnets) requiring specialized training the researcher lacks
risks: Disciplinary barrier: Hiring panel will screen heavily for condensed matter physics credentials. Creative Multimedia + XR background will not survive initial review
Knowledge mismatch: First-principles DFT, spin dynamics, and topological magnetism represent a steep learning curve orthogonal to researcher's existing expertise

Career pivot damage: Accepting a physics research position would signal complete departure from HCI and immersive systems. Future applications to HCI groups would face credibility questions about commitment and identity
Institutional isolation: KTH Department of Applied Physics is not part of the HCI or immersive systems research ecosystem. Limited networking value for future HCI career
